doctorIntro.name: Dr. Anthony Hoang
doctorIntro.bio:
Dr. Anthony Hoang is a Long Beach and Lakewood native who considers it a genuine privilege to practice dentistry in the community where he grew up. After graduating from Lakewood High School, he went on to earn his undergraduate degree from UC Irvine before receiving his DMD from Tufts University School of Dental Medicine in Boston in 2014. He then completed a General Practice Residency at the Loma Linda VA Medical Center, where he honed his skills providing comprehensive dental care to those who served our country.

What drives Dr. Hoang every day is the human side of dentistry — the relationships he builds with patients and the trust they place in him, visit after visit. He has a special gift for putting nervous patients at ease, creating an environment where comfort and quality care go hand in hand. Whether you're coming in for a routine cleaning or a more involved procedure, Dr. Hoang is committed to making sure you feel heard, respected, and well cared for.

At Spring St. Dentistry, Dr. Hoang brings that same hometown dedication to every appointment. He looks forward to getting to know each patient personally and delivering the high-quality, comprehensive dentistry that this community deserves.

faqs.heading: Your Questions About Spring St. Dentistry, Answered
faqs.subheading: From booking your first visit to understanding your treatment options, here's what Long Beach patients ask Dr. Hoang most often.

items.q: How do I schedule an appointment with Dr. Hoang?
items.a: You can call Spring St. Dentistry directly at (562) 420-8578 to book an appointment at our Long Beach office. No referral is needed — we welcome new patients for general and cosmetic dental care. Our team will help you find a time that fits your schedule.

items.q: Do you see patients for dental emergencies or same-day concerns?
items.a: Yes, we do our best to accommodate urgent dental needs as quickly as possible. If you're experiencing tooth pain, a broken tooth, or another pressing issue, call us at (562) 420-8578 and let us know it's an emergency. Dr. Hoang and our team will work to get you seen promptly.

items.q: Does Spring St. Dentistry accept dental insurance?
items.a: We work with a variety of dental insurance plans and will help you understand your coverage before treatment begins. We recommend calling our office at (562) 420-8578 to confirm whether we accept your specific plan. For patients without insurance, we're happy to discuss payment options to make your care affordable.

items.q: What should I expect at my first visit?
items.a: Your first appointment typically includes a comprehensive exam with Dr. Hoang, a review of your dental and medical history, and X-rays if needed. This gives Dr. Hoang a full picture of your oral health so he can recommend the right treatment plan for you. Please arrive a few minutes early to complete any new-patient paperwork.

items.q: Am I a good candidate for clear aligners?
items.a: Clear aligners are a popular option for adults and teens looking to straighten their teeth without traditional metal braces. Dr. Hoang will evaluate your bite, spacing, and overall oral health to determine whether clear aligners are right for you. Most mild to moderate alignment issues can be addressed with this treatment.

items.q: What is a deep cleaning, and do I really need one?
items.a: A deep cleaning — also called scaling and root planing — goes below the gumline to remove built-up plaque and tartar that a routine cleaning can't reach. Dr. Hoang may recommend it if there are signs of gum disease, such as gum inflammation, bleeding, or bone loss detected on X-rays. Treating gum disease early helps protect your teeth and overall health long-term.

items.q: What's the difference between a dental crown and a dental bridge?
items.a: A crown is a cap placed over a single damaged or weakened tooth to restore its shape, strength, and appearance. A bridge, on the other hand, replaces one or more missing teeth by anchoring an artificial tooth to the natural teeth on either side of the gap. Dr. Hoang will recommend the best option based on your specific situation during your exam.

items.q: How do I take care of my teeth after a filling, bonding, or crown?
items.a: Most restorations — including fillings, dental bonding, and crowns — require no special aftercare beyond your normal brushing and flossing routine. You may experience mild sensitivity for a few days after treatment, which is completely normal. If discomfort persists or something feels off with your bite, contact our office so Dr. Hoang can take a look.
